text: Given that a set of functional dependencies F' holds on a relation r(R), it may be possible to infer that certain other functional dependencies must also hold on the relation. For example, given a schema r(4, B, C), if functional dependencies 4 — B and B — C hold on r, we can infer the functional dependency A — C must also hold on r. This is because, given any value of 4, there can be only one corresponding value for B, and for that value of B, there can only be one corresponding value for C. We study in Section 7.4.1, how to make such inferences. We shall use the notation F* to denote the closure of the set F, that is, the set of all functional dependencies that can be inferred given the set F. F* contains all of the functional dependencies in F.
